תֵּימָן rendered the south side; side is the ASV's supplied generic and the the is supplied, so both join the noun's unit, headed on south, which carries the lexeme (rules 15, 31).

The directive he has a word of its own, On, and is its own unit heading on it (rule 32, which reads such a he by rule 11 as a preposition would be). The directional phrase is the predicate of this verbless clause, so the construction's copula shall be joins it on rule 49's terms, the unit discontinuous around the noun under rule 25. The competing readings are to put shall be on the noun's unit (headed south) or on דֶּגֶל under rule 20; rule 20 directs reading the Hebrew clause for which side is the predicate rather than the English word order, and the definite construct phrase is the subject.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment put the copula shall be on דֶּגֶל, but in דֶּגֶל מַחֲנֵה רְאוּבֵן תֵּימָנָה the definite construct phrase is the subject and the directional is the predicate, so rule 20 sends the copula to the predicate and rule 49 puts it on the locative marker that holds the English On. Rule 20 warns in terms that the copula stands beside the subject in exactly these cases and that the Hebrew, not the English word order, decides.

This brings the verse into line with 2.20, where the same verbless shape gives the copula to the prepositional predicate עָלָיו and leaves מַטֵּה only its own English; 2.3 is the other case, where the participial phrase is the subject and the standard-phrase the predicate.
The alternative of placing shall be on תֵּימָן's own unit, headed south, is named in the s005 note.
